summary.name: ClipRecallBar
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source, keyboard-first clipboard history app for the macOS menu bar that filters as you type and pastes on Return.
use_cases: Recalling recently copied text, images or files on a Mac
Pasting earlier clipboard items with a keyboard-only workflow
Pasting copied text as plain text without formatting
Keeping clipboard history private with no network access
Pinning frequently used snippets so they survive clearing history
summary.what_it_does: ClipRecallBar keeps a clipboard history in the macOS menu bar and opens a compact borderless panel via a configurable global hotkey (default Shift-Command-V on the page), with the search field focused. Typing filters entries case- and diacritic-insensitively, and arrow keys plus Return paste into the previous app; Option-Return pastes as plain text and Command-1 to Command-9 paste a row directly. It captures plain text, RTF, file URLs and images, moves duplicates to the top, and lets you set history size from 20 to 999 entries. Concealed or transient items are not stored, specific apps can be ignored by bundle identifier, and Command-P pins entries. History is stored as local JSON and PNG files, and the page states there are no accounts, servers or network code.
notable: Fully local: history saved as files in Application Support with no network code
Keyboard-first: type to filter, Return to paste, Command-1 to 9 direct paste
Respects concealed/transient pasteboard items and per-app ignore lists
MIT licensed, built with Claude Code as a clean-room reimplementation
caveats: Not notarized with a paid Apple Developer ID, so first launch needs right-click Open or xattr command
Pasting with Command-V requires Accessibility permission; without it the user must press Command-V manually
Has had less human code review than a hand-written app, per the page
